references.text: The psalmist writes "Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord," the direct quote that the crowd shouts in [ref:Sal 118:26|Psalm 118:26]. This is the messianic psalm that underlies the people's praise of Jesus at his entry into Jerusalem.

Jesus himself quotes [ref:Sal 118:26|Psalm 118:26] in [ref:Luk 13:35|Luke 13:35] when he weeps over Jerusalem and says that they will not see him again until they say "Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord." The entry into Jerusalem fulfills this word.

In [ref:Matt 21:9|Matthew 21:9], Matthew's parallel account of the entry is found, where the crowd shouts "Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!" Luke adds the title "king" (βασιλεύς) to emphasize Jesus' kingship.
Mark's parallel account in [ref:Mark 11:9-10|Mark 11:9-10] recounts the crowd's shouts at the entry, with the addition "Blessed is the kingdom that comes, our father David's kingdom."

John's parallel account in [ref:Joh 12:13|John 12:13] tells that the people shouted "Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, the King of Israel!" – here too with the royal title, as in Luke.

The prophecy in [ref:Sak 9:9|Zechariah 9:9] about the king of Zion coming riding on a donkey forms the background for the entire entry scene and for the crowd's praise of Jesus as "the king who comes in the name of the Lord."

The words "peace in heaven and glory in the highest" in Luke 19:38 form a deliberate parallel to the angels' song of praise at Jesus' birth in [ref:Luk 2:14|Luke 2:14]: "Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace." At his birth, peace on earth is proclaimed; at his entry, peace in heaven is proclaimed – reconciliation has been accomplished through Jesus' work.
Paul writes in [ref:Ef 2:14|Ephesians 2:14] that Christ "is our peace," which gives deeper meaning to the cry for "peace in heaven" – Jesus as the coming king brings peace between God and humanity.
The expression "glory in the highest" (δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις) reflects the heavenly praise expressed in [ref:Sal 148:1|Psalm 148:1]: "Praise the Lord from heaven, praise him in the heights!"
